name: Reliance Industries Ltd
about: Reliance was founded by Dhirubhai Ambani and is now promoted and managed by his elder son, Mukesh Dhirubhai Ambani. Ambani's family has about 50% shareholding in the conglomerate.

sections.one_liner: Oil-to-telecom-to-retail conglomerate; key issue is margins slipping to 15% while capex commitments balloon.
business: Four engines: Jio digital (533M subscribers), Retail (20,160 stores), Oil-to-Chemicals refining/petchem, plus E&P, FMCG (RCPL) and media. [AR FY26] [Q1FY27 call]
Retail is 31.5% of revenue and Digital 15.0%. O2C and Oil & Gas revenue shares are not disclosed. [AR FY26]
Consumer businesses are 55% of group EBITDA per management, so energy is now under half of profit. [Q4FY26 call]
Domestic India dominates retail and digital. O2C sells internationally. FMCG is expanding to 40+ countries via acquisitions. [AR FY26]
financial_snapshot: Jun-26 quarter: revenue Rs 3,09,468cr (+27% YoY), EBITDA Rs 47,517cr, PAT Rs 23,196cr (-24.6% YoY), OPM 15%. [Numbers]
TTM to Jun-26: revenue Rs 11.23 lakh cr, EBITDA Rs 1,83,561cr (16.3% margin), PAT Rs 88,167cr. [Numbers]
Returns are low: ROCE 10.3%, ROE 8.91%. ROCE has stayed at 8-10% for six years despite revenue more than doubling. [Numbers]
Stock trades at Rs 1,155, near its Rs 1,152 low and 28% below the Rs 1,612 high. P/E 20.9, P/B 1.7x, yield 0.51%. [Numbers]
trajectory: Growth has slowed: revenue CAGR is 17.8% over 5 years but only 6.4% over 3 years. PAT CAGR is 12.2% (5y) versus 8.9% (3y). [Numbers]
EBITDA grew from Rs 1,42,318cr (FY23) to Rs 1,79,065cr (FY26), about 7.9% CAGR, slightly ahead of 6.4% revenue CAGR. [Numbers]
FY26 PAT of Rs 95,754cr includes about Rs 8,900cr Asian Paints gain. Excluding it, PAT is about Rs 86,850cr, roughly +7% YoY. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
Quarterly OPM fell from 18% (Jun/Sep-25) to 15% (Mar/Jun-26). Revenue is up 27%, but EBITDA only about 11% YoY. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings fell to Rs 3,50,719cr in FY24, then rose to Rs 4,02,962cr by FY26 (+15%). D/E is steady at 0.44-0.45. [Numbers]
Working-capital days remain negative at -66. The cash cycle swung from -8 to +25 days in FY26, with debtor days rising 16 to 20. [Numbers]
Funding guard-rail is to keep the A- rating and debt ratios. Capex can be phased or shared with partners; no capex number given. [Q1FY27 call] [Q3FY26 call]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT averages 2.07x over 3 years. FY26 CFO was Rs 1,92,113cr against PAT of Rs 95,754cr, so profits convert to cash. [Numbers]
FCF went from -Rs 16,770cr (FY23) to +Rs 70,023cr (FY26), implying FY26 capex of about Rs 1,22,090cr. [Numbers]
Despite Rs 70,023cr FCF, debt rose Rs 28,649cr in FY26. The use of cash (investments, M&A) is not disclosed. [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management's EBITDA of Rs 54,000cr+ is 14% above the reported Rs 47,517cr. The definitional gap is unreconciled in the material. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
The call's 'PAT +6%' versus the reported -24.6% reconciles: excluding the Rs 8,900cr Asian Paints gain from the base gives about +6%. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
O2C EBITDA was up 17%, yet group OPM fell 3 points. Oil-price pass-through and intentional retail margin cuts are diluting the mix. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
Consumer businesses are now 55% of EBITDA, but group ROE is only 8.9%, and Rs 10 lakh cr AI capex exceeds Rs 9.04 lakh cr net worth. [Q4FY26 call] [AR FY26] [Numbers]
guidance: Retail: double absolute EBITDA by FY30, versus FY26 retail EBITDA of Rs 27,034cr. FY27 margin decline is intentional. [Q1FY27 call] [AR FY26]
FMCG: Rs 1 lakh cr revenue by FY30, from Rs 22,000cr in FY26. That needs about 46% CAGR; current annualised run-rate is about Rs 34,400cr. [Q1FY27 call]
New Energy: 40 GWh battery capacity this year, scaling to 120 GWh (up from 100 GWh in Jan), plus 20 GW solar. [Q1FY27 call] [Q3FY26 call]
Gas: KGD6 ceiling price expected to rise at least $1 in H2 FY27. Ethane imports expected substantially above the 1.6Mt design. [Q1FY27 call]
Capex: no number given. The AR shows FY26 capex of Rs 1,44,271cr plus a Rs 10 lakh cr AI data-centre commitment. [Q1FY27 call] [AR FY26]

ledger.delivered: 25M to 28.6M homes over 2 quarters, about 0.6M/month [Q1FY27 call]

ledger.promised: Organic ARPU growth of 5-6% annually without tariff hikes [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: ARPU Rs 215.6, up Rs 7 YoY, about 3.4% [Q1FY27 call]

ledger.promised: JPL IPO in 'next few months' [Q3FY26 call]; 'fairly imminent' [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: No listing disclosed by the Jul-26 call; not discussed then

ledger.promised: First 40 GWh battery factory starting early next year [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Jul-26: 'will achieve 40 GWh this year', so the start slipped [Q1FY27 call]

ledger.promised: First HJT PV cell line commissioning 'next month' [Q2FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Apr-26 says factories commissioning 'next few quarters'; cell line start not disclosed [Q4FY26 call]

ledger.promised: Fuel cracks stay strong for some time [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: O2C EBITDA +17%, but group OPM fell to 15% from 18% [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]

ledger.promised: More than double beverage capacity; Kurnool plant ready by Mar-26 [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: FMCG revenue Rs 8,600cr, about 2x YoY; capacity figure not disclosed [Q1FY27 call]

ledger.promised: PVC and polyester projects complete by next year end [Q2FY26 call]

bull: FCF quadrupled from about Rs 17,000cr negative to Rs 70,023cr positive in 3 years, with CFO at 2x PAT. [Numbers]
Jio has 285M 5G users, 78% of FWA net adds and ARPU up 3.4% without tariff hikes. A tariff hike is untapped upside. [Q1FY27 call]
At 1.7x book near the 52-week low, a $1 gas price rise and strong cracks offer near-term earnings support. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
bear: OPM fell to 15% for two quarters. EBITDA growth of about 11% trails revenue growth of 27%, and retail margins will fall further by design. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
The Rs 10 lakh cr AI commitment exceeds net worth on a 10% ROCE base, with no capex guidance given. [AR FY26] [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
Execution has slipped on homes, ARPU, IPO timing and battery start. Hormuz, freight running 10x normal, and Qatar LNG force majeure add risk. [Q1FY27 call] [Q4FY26 call]
questions: Reconcile the Rs 54,000cr EBITDA you quoted with the reported Rs 47,517cr.
Debt rose Rs 28,649cr despite Rs 70,023cr FCF. Where did the cash go?
What is the FY27 capex and the phasing of the Rs 10 lakh cr AI spend?
What is the new JPL IPO date, and why did 'next few months' slip?

analyst_pushback.response: Scope for more monetization but careful on forward guidance. Margins improve with scale.

analyst_pushback.response: ARPU not under pressure. Homes mix lower than mobility; 4-5% organic improvement ongoing.

analyst_pushback.response: Minimum 12 months. Discipline on unit economics required. Pull back if assumptions fail.

analyst_pushback.response: Cannot specify capex. Framework: maintain ratings, debt ratios. Flexibility to phase, evaluate partners.

Serves 524M+ digital customers, 387M retail customers, and consumers across 40+ countries through connectivity, retail, branded products, and energy solutions.

annual_report.revenue_mix: India-dominant: retail and digital services concentrated domestically. O2C and oil/gas have international footprint. Consumer products expanding to 40+ countries including Australia, UK, Europe via acquisitions.
strategy: Build sovereign AI infrastructure with ₹10 lakh crore investment for multi-GW data centres
Scale hyperlocal commerce through integrated omnichannel retail ecosystem
Accelerate RCPL through organic expansion, strategic M&A, and global brand building
Maximize O2C returns via operational excellence and optimized feedstock sourcing
Leverage diversified portfolio to navigate macroeconomic volatility
annual_report.outlook: India's consumption environment structurally attractive with favorable demographics and improving incomes. Digital economy growing to $1T by 2030. Organized retail penetration rising. RCPL revenues expected multifold growth by 2030.
annual_report.capex_plans: FY2026: ₹1,44,271 crore directed to O2C, New Energy, Digital Services, and Retail. Additional ₹10 lakh crore committed for AI-ready data centre development.
risks: Trade uncertainties, regional conflicts, geopolitical disruptions impacting supply chains and investment sentiment
Macroeconomic volatility affecting consumer discretionary spending and energy market cyclicality
Limited quality real estate availability for retail store expansion in key markets
Input cost inflation and talent acquisition/retention challenges amid aggressive hyperlocal scaling
annual_report.flags: Material Related Party Transactions of Company and Subsidiaries approved at AGM (Items 6-7). Directors Akash M. Ambani and Anant M. Ambani retiring by rotation. S&P upgraded rating from BBB+ to A- in December 2025.
